question: What are the end products of the catalytic converter reaction?
solution:
The correct answer is __H2O, CO2, N2**(Option 3)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Catalytic converters__ are used in vehicles to reduce harmful emissions.
 
• The catalytic converter facilitates chemical reactions that convert toxic gases into less harmful substances.
 
• It transforms hydrocarbons (HC), carbon monoxide (CO), and nitrogen oxides (NOx) into water (H2O), carbon dioxide (CO2), and nitrogen (N2).
 
• The process involves oxidation and reduction reactions using precious metal catalysts like platinum, palladium, and rhodium.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Emission reduction technologies:**

 
 
• Catalytic converters are part of a vehicle's exhaust system designed to meet emission standards.
 
• They play a key role in protecting the environment by reducing air pollution.
 
 
 
• **Precious metals:**
 
 
• Platinum, palladium, and rhodium are used as catalysts in the converter.
 
• These metals facilitate the conversion of harmful gases into benign substances.
 
 
 
• **Maintenance:**
 
 
• Regular maintenance ensures the catalytic converter functions efficiently.
 
• Failure to maintain can lead to increased emissions and reduced engine performance.
